segments.text: a captain marches ten soldiers into a town hall, and arrests the mayor.
Then he orders the treasurer to hand over the town's cash: over {4,000|four thousand} marks.
The soldiers obey. The mayor obeys. Everyone obeys the uniform.
Then the captain walks out with the money, and simply vanishes.
Except, there is no captain. The man in the uniform is an out-of-work shoemaker with a prison record.
The uniform? Second-hand, from a shop. The soldiers? Ten men who happened to be passing, ordered to follow him.
Ten days later, the police catch him. The sentence: four years in prison.
But after less than two, the Kaiser himself, reportedly amused, pardons him.
And the shoemaker? He goes on tour, playing the captain on stage.
